passage: Tejas had not handed in anything for two weeks. At the team meeting the others exchanged looks and the room felt tight. I could have said, "Tejas, where's your part?" in front of everyone. Instead I waited until after class and walked with him to the gate. "I'm not checking up on you," I said. "I just wondered if something's in the way." Tejas looked at his shoes and said the model needed card, glue and paint, and there was none at home. I hadn't guessed that at all. I asked whether he would take the research and the report, which needed only a library book and a notebook, and let Anita handle the materials. His shoulders came down. Two days later he brought four pages of notes. I'm Chandrika, and I'm glad I asked quietly.

qa.q: What did Tejas say was in the way?
qa.a: Tejas said the model needed card, glue and paint, and there was none at home.

qa.q: How did Tejas feel when Chandrika asked quietly at the gate?
qa.a: Tejas felt embarrassed at first, looking at his shoes, then relieved, as his shoulders came down.

qa.q: What else could Chandrika do to help Tejas feel part of the team, and why?
qa.a: Chandrika could ask Tejas to present the research at the next check-in, because owning a real part lets Tejas show what Tejas contributes.

qa.q: How might the other team members have seen Tejas's silence before the talk?
qa.a: They probably thought Tejas did not care and felt annoyed, since nobody knew the real reason.

grounding: The leader speaks privately to the quiet member, asks what is blocking him, finds he lacks materials, and shifts him to research he can do at home, without shaming him in front of others.

passage:
Note from the art teacher, Class 8 clay model project

In week two I noticed the group led by Ishita working around one boy. Sachin sat at the end of the table, hands in his lap, while the others shaped the clay village. Twice a girl in the group said loudly, "Some people do nothing."

After class I saw Ishita wait for him at the door. She did not scold him in front of anyone. From my desk I heard her ask, "Is something stopping you?" He was quiet, then said he had no clay or tools at home and felt stupid asking.

The next day Ishita changed his job. He would research how village houses stay cool and write the display card, which he could do at home. His card was the best-written in the class.

I have added shared clay kits to the art room.

qa.q: What did Sachin say was stopping him?
qa.a: He said he had no clay or tools at home and felt stupid asking.

qa.q: How was Sachin feeling before Ishita spoke to him?
qa.a: He felt ashamed and left out, sitting with his hands in his lap and too embarrassed to ask for materials.

qa.q: What else could the group have done besides changing Sachin's job?
qa.a: They could have shared their own clay and tools during class, so he could still take part in the hands-on work.

qa.q: How might the girl who said "Some people do nothing" see Sachin now?
qa.a: She might feel a bit sheepish, realising he was blocked by missing materials, not laziness, once his card turned out the best.

grounding: A teacher's note shows a leader speaking privately to a non-contributing member, learning he lacks materials and shifting him to research he can do at home.

subtype: Approach: handling a member who is not contributing [Action]
passage:
Wednesday

Jeevan has done nothing on our history poster for two weeks. Arjit and Farheen keep saying I should complain to Sir. Today Farheen said, loud enough for Jeevan to hear, "Passenger."

I didn't want to do it like that. After the bell I caught Jeevan near the cycle stand, away from everyone, and just asked what's going on.

He looked at his shoes for a while. Then he said his family moved into his uncle's place, there's no printer, and he can't stay after school because he picks up his little sister. He thought if he said it, we'd laugh.

So we switched. He'll do the research on the 1857 uprising at home, just reading and writing notes, and send photos of them. Arjit will print. Jeevan actually smiled.

I'm Kunal, and I'm glad I didn't just report him.

qa.q: Why can't Jeevan stay after school?
qa.a: He picks up his little sister after school.

qa.q: What was Jeevan feeling when he looked at his shoes?
qa.a: Jeevan felt ashamed and worried that the group would laugh at his situation.

qa.q: What else could Kunal do to protect Jeevan from the teasing?
qa.a: Kunal could quietly ask Farheen to stop the name-calling, so Jeevan is not shamed in front of the group.

qa.q: How might Arjit see the new arrangement?
qa.a: Arjit may feel relieved and more patient, now that the work is moving and the reason Jeevan was stuck is clear.

grounding: A diary shows a leader privately asking a quiet member what is blocking him, finding he lacks resources and shifting him to research he can do at home.
